Traditional Roast Goose

Served at: St. Martin's Day (Martinstag) · Christmas Day

Serves 6-8Prep 30 minCook 2 hr 30 min

Roast Goose is a classic centerpiece for St. Martin's Day (Martinstag) and Christmas Day celebrations in many European households, especially in Germany. This rich and flavorful dish symbolizes abundance and festivity, often served with seasonal sides like red cabbage and dumplings.

Ingredients

  • 1 whole goose (10-12 lbs / 4.5-5.5 kg), thawed if frozen
  • 2 teaspoons salt
  • 1 teaspoon black pepper
  • 1 large apple, quartered
  • 1 large onion, quartered
  • 2 sprigs fresh thyme
  • 2 sprigs fresh rosemary
  • 1 cup (240 ml) chicken or vegetable broth
  • 1 tablespoon honey (optional)
  • 1 tablespoon apple cider vinegar (optional)

Method

  1. Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
  2. Remove any giblets from the goose cavity and pat the goose dry with paper towels.
  3. Prick the skin all over with a sharp fork or skewer, being careful not to pierce the meat, to help render the fat during roasting.
  4. Season the goose inside and out with salt and black pepper.
  5. Stuff the cavity with the quartered apple, onion, thyme, and rosemary.
  6. Place the goose breast-side up on a rack in a large roasting pan.
  7. Roast the goose for about 2 hours, basting occasionally with the rendered fat.
  8. After 2 hours, pour off excess fat from the pan (reserve for other cooking if desired).
  9. Brush the skin with honey mixed with apple cider vinegar if using, to encourage browning and a slight glaze.
  10. Increase the oven temperature to 400°F (200°C) and roast for an additional 20-30 minutes until the skin is crisp and golden brown and the internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C) in the thickest part of the thigh.
  11. Remove the goose from the oven and let it rest for 15-20 minutes before carving.
  12. While the goose rests, pour the pan drippings into a saucepan, add broth, and simmer to make a flavorful gravy if desired.

Tips

  • Pricking the skin helps to render out excess fat, which goose has plenty of, resulting in crispy skin.
  • Save the rendered goose fat for roasting potatoes or vegetables; it adds wonderful flavor.
  • Serve with traditional sides such as red cabbage, potato dumplings, or braised apples for an authentic festive meal.
